<!-- page 684 -->

|**Why this issue is important**|Probability of stopping treatment for any reason should reflect what would normally happen in<br>clinical practice as closely as possible. Otherwise the length of time for which treatment is taken may<br>not be accurate, which may affect the costs and effectiveness of treatment.|
|---|---|
|**Technical team preliminary**<br>**judgement and rationale**|The 5% stopping rate used by the ERG is based on the UK MS Risk Sharing Scheme that only<br>included beta-interferons and glatiramer acetate. It is unclear whether the same probability of<br>stopping treatment for any reason should apply to newer disease-modifying therapies and for all<br>years. The company should provide a scenario analysis altering the stopping rates for individual<br>treatments based on available evidence.|
|**Summary of comments**|**Comments received from company:**<br><br>Company prefers stopping rates from pivotal trials for each disease modifying therapy<br>because of significant differences between treatments with respect to safety and adverse<br>event profile. A scenario analysis using the same probability of stopping for all therapies<br>(5%) consistent with previous appraisals show that peginterferon beta-1a remains a cost-<br>effective option.<br>**Comments received from clinical expert:**<br><br>In the absence of evidence, it is not plausible to apply the same probability of stopping<br>treatment for all therapies because side effects differ substantially and some may be time-<br>dependent.<br><br>Probability of stopping treatment will be relatively high initially because of side effects but<br>because of the disease progression to SPMS, probability of stopping treatment after several<br>years will increase again.<br>**Comments received from clinical organisation:**<br><br>It is not plausible to apply the same probability of stopping treatment because different<br>treatments have different efficacies and tolerances and some therapies (alemtuzumab and<br>cladribine) are time-limited (18 to 24 months).<br><br>The probabilities of stopping treatment in the table are plausible but this is an area of<br>uncertainty.|



Technical report – Peginterferon beta-1a for treating relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis Issue date: November 2019 





<!-- page 685 -->

||**Comments received from patient organisations:**<br><br>It is not clinically plausible to apply the same probability of stopping treatment because<br>different disease modifying therapies are different classes of drugs, are administered<br>differently and at different times.<br>**Comments received from comparator company:**<br><br>It is not clinically plausible to model stopping rates being the same over time for all disease<br>modifying therapies. Alemtuzumab cannot be meaningfully stopped after 2 years as it is no<br>longer taken but it is not expected to be efficacious indefinitely as it is not curative.<br><br>Stopping rates are unlikely to be constant over time with early stopping driven by intolerance<br>and later stopping reflecting lack of efficacy. In appraisal on daclizumab (TA441 now<br>withdrawn), the committee preferred a model with separate rates for Years 1, 2 and 3+.|
|---|---|
|**Technical team judgement after**<br>**engagement**|It is clinically more plausible that individual disease modifying therapies would have specific<br>stopping rates, which will likely vary over time.|



## _**Issue 7 – Utility values**_ 

|**Background/description of issue**|In its base case analysis, the**company**used the utility values fromOrme et al. (2007) for<br>consistency with previous technology appraisals. It also provided utility values from a more recent<br>study,Thompson et al. (2017),although these were not used in any company analyses.<br>The**ERG**provided a scenario analysis using Thompson et al. (2017). This study collected resource<br>use, cost and health-related quality of life (EQ-5D) data in a cross-sectional retrospective study of<br>779 people living in the UK with multiple sclerosis. The ERG highlighted that this study includes<br>information collected from people receiving treatment with more recent disease-modifying therapies,<br>but that the participants were older than those in the Orme study and had fewer people. On the<br>whole, the utility values in each health state are similar. However there are some health states<br>where the differences are more pronounced, for example, Expanded Disability Status Scale (EDSS)|

<!-- page 687 -->

- appraisals. A scenario analysis using Thompson study showed that peginterferon beta-1a remains a cost-effective option. 

## **Comments received from clinical expert:** 

- Just over 30% of patients in the cohorts included in Orme and Thompson had RRMS and the rest had progressive MS; 25% have primary progressive MS and would not be prescribed interferons. Neither cohorts are representative of patients likely to start interferons, although a subset (patients with RRMS and lower EDSS scores) will be more representative. 

- From a clinical perspective, there have been substantial changes in referral patterns and increasing treatment options, both of which may affect care cost estimates, and so it seems logical to use more recently acquired data. 

## **Comments received from clinical organisation:** 

- On balance, Thompson et al is the preferred study for utility data. 

## **Comments received from patient organisation:** 

- Orme has been the standard for previous appraisals so it would be more consistent to follow previous practice. 

## **Comments received from comparator company:** 

- The sample size in Orme is 2.5 times larger than Thompson. Orme has been used in many previous MS appraisals allowing for consistency in decision making. 

- There are issues regarding face validity of the higher utility values for patients in EDSS 7 health state (people who have become wheelchair bound) and EDSS 8 health state (people who have become bed-ridden for life) reported by Thompson. 

- Orme also provides utilities for SPMS and relapse, whereas Thompson does not. The ERG applies Thompson data and continues to apply parts of the Orme regression analysis directly to the Thompson data which may not be valid. 

Technical report – Peginterferon beta-1a for treating relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis Issue date: November 2019 





<!-- page 688 -->

**Technical team judgement after engagement** 

Utility values are broadly similar between the 2 studies, and using Orme et al. is consistent with previous appraisals. 

Technical report – Peginterferon beta-1a for treating relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis Issue date: November 2019
